Article Title: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow amid one-fifth cut to 2026 spending forecast
Article Text:
Tesla cuts 2026 capex by one fifth

SpaceX merger puts Tesla's spending under scrutiny

Revenue beats estimates, but net income plunges 43%

FSD adoption and automotive margins improve

Tesla reported an unexpected $1.53 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter, beating Wall Street's expectations, as the electric vehicle maker spent less than anticipated on capital expenditure.However, a one-fifth cut to its 2026 spending forecast has raised questions about its investment plans for artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and autonomous driving. The company now expects capital expenditure of around $20 billion in 2026, down from its earlier forecast of more than $25 billion. Tesla did not specify which areas would see lower spending.In the quarter ended September 30, Tesla spent $4.7 billion on capital expenditure, double the amount spent a year earlier but well below the $7.5 billion analysts had expected on average, according to LSEG data.The lower spending helped Tesla report free cash flow of $1.53 billion, compared with market expectations of a cash outflow of $4.92 billion.Tesla's shares initially rose 2% in after-hours trading after the results, supported by positive free cash flow, higher gross margins and revenue that exceeded Wall Street expectations. However, the stock reversed direction to trade 2% lower. Shares have fallen around 14% this year."The free cash flow beat was a pleasant surprise, but when combined with the lower-than-expected capex, raises questions on the next step for the automaker," said Ryan Lee, senior vice president of product and strategy at Direxion, which offers exchange-traded funds tied to Tesla. "Lower capex suggests less of an 'all-in' approach to the AI arms race than one would expect from Elon."The results come as chief executive Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX, his space venture. The unexpected cash generation could strengthen Tesla's financial position ahead of a possible deal, but lower investment in AI, robotaxis and humanoid robots could raise concerns about its ability to deliver on its growth ambitions.On Tuesday, Musk described a merger between the two companies as a "good idea" and said they had formed special committees to discuss the proposal. He declined to provide further details during Wednesday's conference call with analysts.A combination would bring together businesses central to Musk's long-term vision of an integrated technology and manufacturing group spanning AI, energy, robotics, communications and transportation on Earth and beyond.However, investors will want to see whether Tesla is investing enough to turn Musk's ambitions into commercial businesses, particularly as the robotaxi rollout has lagged behind his promises."The merger still faces a high bar, but tonight’s numbers make the financial logic harder to ignore," said Thomas Monteiro, a senior analyst at Investing.com."The main takeaway is that Tesla's surprisingly positive cash flow quarter did not come from stronger profits, but from spending billions less than planned at a time when SpaceX is preparing to invest up to $40 billion in a single quarter."Tesla's financial performance presented a mixed picture. Revenue remained flat compared with a year earlier, despite the end of US tax credits that had supported sales in the previous year. Nevertheless, the figure exceeded Wall Street's expectations.Net income fell 43% during the quarter.Tesla said it had ended the quarter with its largest backlog of passenger vehicles in four years. Higher petrol prices have supported demand for electric vehicles, particularly in Europe.The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, putting it on track to increase annual deliveries for the first time in three years."Demand is growing rapidly for our vehicles. It's exceeding our production by a significant margin," Musk said on the conference call with analysts. "In a nutshell, after many years of sort of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we're now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth."Tesla also reported stronger adoption of its driver-assistance technology in North America. The FSD (supervised) attach rate exceeded three-quarters of new vehicle deliveries, an increase of nearly 20 percentage points from the second quarter, the company said.Automotive gross margin, excluding regulatory credits, reached 18.1% in the third quarter, above analysts' estimate of 16.7%, according to Visible Alpha data.Tesla's energy business has recently helped offset pressures on its automotive operations. The latter remain under scrutiny as competitors worldwide launch newer, often cheaper models. Tesla continues to rely heavily on its ageing Model 3 and Model Y.Despite the competitive pressures, Tesla aims to produce five million vehicles annually by around 2030, compared with an expected 2.5 million this year.
Article Summary: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow, beating Wall Street's expectations. Company cuts 2026 capex forecast by one fifth to $20 billion, down from $25 billion. Results come as CEO Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX.

Article Title: Rupee under pressure: Currency slips to 94.50 as oil rises, Dalal Street struggles in red
Article Text:
Rupee gives up some gains

NEW DELHI: Rupee weakened in early trade on Thursday, losing 12 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar as rising crude oil prices and a decline in the equity market weighed down the currency. A softer dollar and lower US treasury yields, however, helped limit the fall.The currency opened at 94.47 at the interbank foreign exchange market before slipping to 94.50. The decline came a day after the rupee had climbed 53 paise to close at 94.38 against the dollar on Wednesday.Forex analysts said the rupee was trading on a flat-to-lower note amid pressure from the domestic stock market and higher oil prices. The dollar’s weakness and easing US Treasury yields offered some support to the currency.Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, expects rupee to retain a slight positive bias."We expect the rupee to trade with a slight positive bias on IPO related foreign inflows and weakness in the dollar. Softening of US treasury yields and reports that Russia is ready for new peace talks may also support the rupee," he told PTI.Choudhary added that market participants would track the weekly unemployment claims data from the US for further direction.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six currencies, fell 0.21 per cent to 101.56. In contrast, Brent crude futures rose 1.58 per cent to $110.54 per barrel.Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research at Kotak NEO, said the rupee remained finely balanced within the 94-97 range."The RBI has bought itself time, the Jio IPO has added near-term dollar supply, and a US trade agreement could strengthen the structural inflow story. But if portfolio selling accelerates again or crude makes a decisive move towards $120, that balance will be tested," Banerjee added.The domestic equity market also remained under pressure during early trade. BSE Sensex dropped 642.51 points to 73,067.18, while NSE Nifty50 declined 241.35 points to 22,570.90.Despite the weakness in equities on Thursday morning, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were net buyers in the previous session. They purchased equities worth Rs 1,022.32 crore on Wednesday, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee loses 12 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday. Rising crude oil prices and a decline in the equity market weighed down the currency. A softer dollar and lower US treasury yields, however, helped limit the fall. The decline came a day after the rupee had climbed 53 paise against the dollar.

Article Title: Brent crude tops $110 as fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia raise concerns over oil supplies
Article Text:
Crude prices hold above $110 per barrel

Shipping risks extend beyond Strait of Hormuz

US crude inventories fall, distillate stocks rise

Oil prices edged higher on Thursday, with Brent crude trading above $110 a barrel. The rise came after fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted US to order some diplomats and their family members to leave American missions in the Kingdom.At the same time, concerns over shipping safety and oil supplies in the region also persisted.WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%.US officials told Reuters that the state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region.The latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday. At least one person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on a civilian airport in Dammam. A drone attack on a Saudi oil field killed two people.Explosions were also reported in Sirik, in southern Iran, on Wednesday. Iranian media said that the nature and origin of the blasts were unknown.The threat to energy supplies has extended to maritime routes beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler data showed at least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks.LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting tankers further afield, including in the Gulf of Oman. Such attacks were jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers that support regional loadings.Iran's leadership also issued fresh statements amid the tensions. Foreign minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times on Wednesday that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself. President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.US crude inventories declined by 3.06 million barrels last week to 412.5 million barrels, according to data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Wednesday. The fall was greater than the 820,000-barrel draw expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.Distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, increased by 1.68 million barrels to 104.3 million barrels during the week. Analysts had expected these stockpiles to fall by 1.16 million barrels, EIA data showed.Separately, the Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the US emergency heating oil reserve, which holds one million barrels. The department of energy announced the move on Wednesday as the administration seeks to contain prices that have risen amid diesel shortages linked to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.Elsewhere, Russian President Vladimir Putin met US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The meeting came as Washington renewed efforts to end Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.The Kremlin said Putin had agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy backed the proposed talks and said he hoped they would begin as soon as possible.
Article Summary: WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%. US state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region. Latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday.

Article Title: Amid volatile trades, sensex falls for 4th day
Article Text:
During the day’s session, sensex fluctuated by more than 1,300 points but closed just 126 points down at 73,124 points.

MUMBAI: Rising crude oil prices and a weakening rupee weighed on investor sentiment on Friday and led to strong volatility in the market. But at close, the two leading indices—sensex and Nifty—were only marginally lower. Midcap and smallcap stocks, however, witnessed heavy selling and closed deep in the red.During the day’s session, sensex fluctuated by more than 1,300 points but closed just 126 points down at 73,124 points. Nifty on NSE also witnessed strong volatility and closed 88 points lower at 22,600 points, mainly because of foreign fund buying in the latter half of the session, market players said. Outside of the main indices, BSE’s midcap index closed 2.2% lower while the smallcap index closed 2.5%.The day’s slide came despite Rs 888-crore net buying by foreign funds and another Rs 3,235-crore net buying by domestic institutions, BSE data showed. Early on Friday, Brent crude had hit a nearly six-month high at $114 per barrel. As a result, the rupee also weakened and inched closer to the 95-to-a-dollar mark again and closed at 94.93.According to Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments, the key concern in Friday’s market was the disproportionately sharp correction in mid and smallcap stocks relative to the leading indices. “Valuation concerns and unwinding of leveraged positions, combined with surging crude prices and weak global cues, have intensified pressure on the broader market. The rise in India VIX also indicates that near-term volatility will persist,” Nair said.“Continued tensions (in West Asia) could keep crude prices high, while the AI-led global equity sell-off continues to weigh on risk appetite.”
Article Summary: Sensex fluctuated by more than 1,300 points but closed just 126 points down at 73,124 points. Nifty on NSE also witnessed strong volatility and closed 88 points lower at 22,600 points. Midcap and smallcap stocks, however, witnessed heavy selling and closed deep in the red.

Article Title: At $43 billion, RBI’s net dollar purchase hits new high
Article Text:
Purchase Up 94% Since July.

Surges 132% In Aug Driven By FCNR Flows,Forward Liabilities Rise Too, Cross $200Bn

MUMBAI: RBI’s net dollar purchases surged 132% to $43.3 billion in Aug 2026, driven by inflows through its concessional FCNR(B) swap facility, while its outstanding net forward short position crossed $200 billion for the first time.RBI bought $74.5 billion in dollars during the month, up 93.9% from $38.4 billion in July. It made no dollar purchases in Aug 2025, when it was defending the rupee amid foreign portfolio outflows. Dollar sales rose 57.9% month-on-month to $31.2 billion from $19.8 billion in July and were 305.6% higher than the $7.7 billion sold in Aug 2025.Net purchases were 132% higher than the $18.7 billion recorded in July and contrasted with net sales of $7.7 billion in Aug 2025. Gross transactions across onshore and offshore over-the-counter markets exceeded $105.7 billion. RBI’s dollar purchases helped absorb the $127 billion mobilised by banks through FCNR(B) deposits from NRIs.However, pressure on the rupee prompted the central bank to sell dollars to support the currency. Its dollar sales of $31.2 billion in Aug represented around a quarter of the amount mobilised through FCNR(B) deposits, though the two figures cover different types of transactions and periods of currency management.India’s foreign exchange reserves fell by $5.01 billion to $721.02 billion in the week ended Oct 16, down $64.7 billion from their all-time high of $785.71 billion in the week ended Sept 4, as pressure on the rupee continued. Foreign currency assets, the largest component of reserves, declined by $5.76 billion during the latest week. The fall was partly offset by a $706 million increase in the value of gold reserves.RBI’s concessional dollar-rupee swap facility allowed banks to exchange dollar deposits raised from NRIs for three to five years for rupees, while securing forward hedges from the central bank. The deposit mobilisation window closed at the end of Aug, prompting banks to surrender the dollar proceeds to RBI.The central bank also stepped up dollar sales and conducted offsetting sellbuy swaps to manage the rupee and the liquidity injected through its purchases. Its outstanding net forward short position rose by $63.3 billion, or 46.3%, in a month to a record $200.1 billion at end-Aug, compared with $136.8 billion in July and $53.4 billion a year earlier.
Article Summary: RBI bought $74.5 billion in dollars during the month, up 93.9% from $38.4 billion in July. Outstanding net forward short position crossed $200 billion for the first time. Gross transactions across onshore and offshore over-the-counter markets exceeded $105.7 billion.

Article Title: From fuel price hikes to cost-of-living concerns, US consumer sentiment nears record low
Article Text:
File photo: A shopper looks at the section of a grocery store in Fort Worth, Texas (Picture credit: AP)

Independent voters report weaker sentiment

Inflation expectations remain elevated

Federal Reserve decision due next week

US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices linked to the Middle East conflict weighed on households' views of the economy, a University of Michigan survey showed on Friday, with affordability emerging as a key issue ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The university's Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September.Economists polled by Reuters had expected a reading of 46.3, which was also the preliminary estimate for October.October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began."Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10% below a year ago and 15% less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict."The survey's findings coincided with political polling showing that voters held a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's handling of it, Reuters reported.Millions of Americans have already cast early ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress for the final two years of Trump's term.Polls indicated Republicans were likely to lose control of the House of Representatives, with the Senate also potentially at stake. Trump's approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll stood at a record low, amid a surge in fuel prices following his decision to attack Iran in late February.The University of Michigan survey found that the decline in sentiment was driven by respondents who identified as independents, a group that includes swing voters.Their sentiment score fell to 42.4 in October from 47.7 in September, putting it just above May's record low of 40.6. Sentiment scores among Democrats and Republicans improved.The survey also found that more independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents reporting inflation pressures as a financial burden had risen by 27%, while the figure among Republicans had increased by 52%. Among Democrats, the increase was 15%.Households with little or no exposure to the stock market had also increasingly cited high prices as a financial burden compared with the beginning of the year. The stock market had recently climbed rapidly amid enthusiasm for investments in artificial intelligence.The survey's measure of consumers' expectations for inflation over the next 12 months rose to 4.7% in October from 4.6% in September. The measure had stood at 3.4% in February, before the US-Israeli war with Iran began.Expectations for inflation over the next five years increased to 3.5% from 3.4% in September and 3.2% in March, shortly after the conflict began.In an accompanying report, Hsu said persistently elevated inflation expectations in the period following the Covid-19 pandemic posed a risk to the Federal Reserve's efforts to bring inflation down to its 2% target. The target had remained unmet for more than five years, she wrote."Consumers broadly expect inflation to accelerate, and this year’s increases in inflation expectations are not limited to one part of the political spectrum," Hsu said.She also cautioned that relatively resilient consumer spending, despite negative views of the economy, required close attention. If households were spending now to avoid expected price increases in the future, bringing inflation down could become more difficult, she added.Federal Reserve officials are scheduled to meet in Washington next week. Despite recent inflation readings that came in higher than expected, they were broadly expected to keep the policy interest rate unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%.The Fed had raised the rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September. Most officials had indicated a need for higher interest rates, while key policymakers had also expressed willingness to wait for more data before making their next move.
Article Summary: Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September. October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began. More independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances.

Article Title: Upper layer NBFCs have to list: RBI governor on Tatas; dispels doubts on Sept order
Article Text:
The remarks appear to settle a debate sparked by Noel Tata, chair of Tata Trusts.

“NBFCs and CICs, like for example Tata Sons and others, are required to be registered with us because of the systemic risks,” Malhotra said.

‘CICs sit atop group cos, can leverage funds through them’

Mumbai: In his first public comment since Reserve Bank of India rejected Tata Sons’ bid to shed its non-bank lender status, governor Sanjay Malhotra on Friday left little doubt that the Tata Group holding company must list publicly as long as it remains classified as an upper-layer (UL) non-banking financial company (NBFC) and core investment company (CIC).The remarks appear to settle a debate sparked by Noel Tata, chair of Tata Trusts, Tata Sons’ largest shareholder, who had argued that RBI’s Sept 11 order, which rejected the holding company’s request to deregister as a CIC and directed it to comply with UL-NBFC regulations, did not explicitly mandate a listing.Malhotra’s comments also suggest Tata Sons is in breach of RBI rules. The consequences of continued noncompliance remain unclear.The governor declined to be drawn into the question of Noel Tata’s proposal to merge two Tata Sons subsidiaries with the holding company, a move that could help it sidestep a stock market listing.“NBFCs and CICs, like for example Tata Sons and others, are required to be registered with us because of the systemic risks,” Malhotra said.“As long as it is an NBFC within our definition, it’s a CIC and has access to funds direct or indirect, it’s required to be registered and if it is in the upper layer, it is required to list,” he said at NDTV’s World Summit conference Friday.RBI first classified Tata Sons as an UL-NBFC in 2022 and required it to list within three years. The holding company sought to avoid a market debut by applying to surrender its CIC registration after reducing its debt to zero. But in Sept, the central bank rejected the request, saying it “cannot be acceded to”.RBI requires UL-NBFCs with assets exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore, or direct or indirect access to public funds, to list. With assets of Rs 2.01 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026, Tata Sons comfortably exceeds the threshold. Malhotra said CICs sit atop group companies and can leverage funds through them, exposing money raised from banks, corporate bonds and other sources to risk.Days after receiving the RBI letter, the Tata Sons board discussed the regulator’s decision at its Sept 17 meeting and agreed to comply with RBI regulations, but did not take a call on listing.Noel Tata, who is also a director of Tata Sons, has asked the company to explore alternatives to a market debut. He told the board: “It (the RBI’s communique) does not mention listing. It prescribes no particular step, and it does not say that the company is in breach.” He added that the board had formed no view on the legal effect of the RBI’s communication or what actions it required Tata Sons to take and by when.
Article Summary: The remarks appear to settle a debate sparked by Noel Tata, chair of Tata Trusts. “NBFCs and CICs, like for example Tata Sons and others, are required to be registered with us because of the systemic risks,” Malhotra said.

Article Title: Record haul: Jio IPO collects Rs 7.5 lakh crore; nearly 1.3 crore investors make bids
Article Text:
In 2008, the Reliance Power IPO had seen the total demand at about Rs 7.1 lakh crore.

Nearly 1.3Cr Investors Make Bids; Institutions Lead Charge

MUMBAI: The maiden public offering for Jio Platforms, which aimed to raise a recordbreaking Rs 30,213 crore, on Friday created several other records. It saw about 1.3 crore retail investors participating in the offer. While the institutional part was subscribed more than 70 times, the total demand for shares, including the anchor part in the offer, touched almost Rs 7.5 lakh crore.The earlier record for applications in an IPO was for Waaree Energies in which a little over 97 lakh investors had applied. In 2008, the Reliance Power IPO had seen the total demand at about Rs 7.1 lakh crore. At Friday’s close of bidding, Jio IPO surpassed both these marks.On Day 1, India’s biggest IPO was fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening, exchange data had shown. By Day 2, the issue was subscribed more than five times. And at the close of Day 3, the last day of the bidding process, the IPO was subscribed 22.2 times, exchange data showed. At close, the institutional (QIB) part of the IPO, in which a little over 4.9 crore shares were offered, was subscribed 70.6 times, while the HNI portion, in which about 3.6 crore shares were reserved, was subscribed 14 times.Exchange data also showed that the portion reserved for Jio employees was subscribed nearly three times while the part reserved for RIL shareholders was subscribed 7.6 times. The portion marked for retail investors, in which about 8.5 crore shares were offered, was subscribed 2.7 times.In the unofficial market, speculators are betting that the company will be listing at about Rs 1,370, a mark-up (also called the grey market premium or GMP) of about Rs 250 over the upper limit of the IPO price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119. The current GMP is slightly off Rs 273, the highest level seen a day before the IPO opened. However, the latest GMP is much higher than the opening quote of Rs 148 on Oct 4, data from websites tracking the price trend in the unofficial market for shares showed.The strong response to the IPO comes on the back of a Rs 2.5-lakh-crore anchor book that was subscribed 30 times its size, which was Rs 8,110 crore, disclosures by the merchant bankers to the issue showed.
Article Summary: The earlier record for applications in an IPO was for Waaree Energies in which a little over 97 lakh investors had applied. In 2008, the Reliance Power IPO had seen the total demand at about Rs 7.1 lakh crore. On Day 1, India’s biggest IPO was fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening.

Article Title: India seventh most targeted by cyberattacks: MS executive Nicholas Butts
Article Text:
AI was also lowering the barriers for smaller criminal operations, he said.

NEW DELHI: India is the world’s seventh most targeted country by cyberattacks and third in Asia, a senior Microsoft executive said Friday, warning that artificial intelligence was already helping criminals mount ransomware and espionage campaigns.At the NDTV World Summit 2026, Nicholas Butts, director of AI and cybersecurity policy at Microsoft, said the risks were immediate.“What we’re seeing is not about potential doom and gloom in 10 years but about very real security threats right here today,” he said.Butts cited Storm 3168, also called Jadepuffer, which he described as a China-based ransomware operation using AI agents against customers worldwide.He also pointed to Russian and Chinese state-sponsored actors deploying agents for espionage, including a group Microsoft tracks as Storm 0940.AI was also lowering the barriers for smaller criminal operations, he said.Butts cited EvilTokens, allegedly built by two individuals using AI coding tools, which offered access to criminal infrastructure and affected more than 10,000 organisations across 120 countries. He did not specify how many were Indian.“The threat is very real to India,” Butts said. Microsoft’s assessment draws on its extensive security monitoring, including screening about five billion emails daily, he added.
Article Summary: India is the world’s seventh most targeted country by cyberattacks and third in Asia. Microsoft executive warns that artificial intelligence was already helping criminals mount ransomware and espionage campaigns. Nicholas Butts, director of AI and cybersecurity policy at Microsoft, said the risks were immediate.

Article Title: India needs to scale up battery storage alongside renewable energy: Experts
Article Text:
India needs to expand battery storage and grid infrastructure alongside renewable energy. (Pic Credit: ANI)

NEW DELHI: India needs to expand battery storage and grid infrastructure alongside renewable energy capacity to ensure reliable power supply as it moves towards its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, experts said at an industry event.The country has crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity, but integrating more renewable power into the grid will require investment in energy storage, domestic manufacturing and research, said Jai Asundi, executive director of the Centre for Study of Science, Technology and Policy (CSTEP).The discussions took place at the Renewable Energy India Expo, held alongside The Battery Show India and the Energy Storage Summit India in Greater Noida.Yogesh Mudras, managing director of Informa Markets in India, said renewable energy generation and grid storage must expand together as India’s clean energy market grows. “We have reached an execution phase where generation and grid storage must scale in tandem,” he said, adding that India’s renewable energy market was projected to reach 486 GW by 2030, while its battery storage sector was expected to cross $8.5 billion by 2031.Anandi Iyer, director of the Fraunhofer Office in India, said the world added around 800 GW of renewable energy capacity in 2025, while global battery storage deployment reached 108 GW, up 40% from the previous year. She said India and Germany could work together in battery research, power electronics and advanced engineering.Australia’s high commissioner to India, Philip Green, said the two countries could combine Australia’s critical mineral resources and solar technology with India’s manufacturing capabilities to strengthen clean energy supply chains. Australia produces more than half of the world’s lithium, he said.Scotland First Minister John Swinney said Scottish expertise and innovation could complement India’s manufacturing scale and market potential to support the clean energy transition.Manu Srivastav, additional chief secretary in Madhya Pradesh’s power and renewable energy department, said falling technology costs and economies of scale were making renewable energy increasingly competitive with conventional power.The three-day event, which opened on Thursday, has over 1,080 exhibitors and 1,400 brands, with participation from more than 10 countries.
Article Summary: India has crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity. Integrating more renewable power into the grid will require investment in energy storage, domestic manufacturing and research. India’s renewable energy market was projected to reach 486 GW by 2030, while its battery storage sector was expected to cross $8.5 billion by 2031.

Article Title: German companies looking for business opportunities: Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
Piyush Goyal said German companies had publicly announced investments worth $7.4 billion in India.

BERLIN: German companies are exploring investment opportunities in India in precision engineering, aerospace, defence and shipbuilding, besides healthcare, pharmaceuticals and research and development, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said, pointing to growing business interest as European firms look to diversify manufacturing and supply chains.Talking to reporters during his visit to Germany and The Netherlands with a delegation of Indian businesses and startups to explore opportunities in trade, investment and industrial cooperation, Goyal said German companies had publicly announced investments worth $7.4 billion in India with some of these already materialising.More than 2,000 German companies currently operate in India, while cumulative German FDI equity inflows stood at $15.6 billion between April 2000 and March 2026.“With all the regulatory overhang that they (EU) are creating upon themselves, European manufacturing will have to look for trusted partner countries where many of the things that are becoming very expensive in Europe can be produced. So I see tremendous potential for India and huge job creation in India,” Goyal said.He said India could also emerge as an important export base for automobiles.
Article Summary: More than 2,000 German companies currently operate in India. cumulative German FDI equity inflows stood at $15.6 billion between April 2000 and March 2026. German companies have publicly announced investments worth $7.4 billion in India with some of these already materialising.

Article Title: Infosys ADRs tumble 6% as growth guidance cut to 1-2%
Article Text:
he slowdown was particularly sharp in high-tech and retail, which declined 17.3% and 7.7% year on year,

BENGALURU: Infosys had a lacklustre Q2, with its shares falling 6% in early trade on the NYSE after it cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% in constant currency terms from 1.5%-3% earlier. This is the company’s weakest growth outlook in seven years, reflecting subdued volumes, pricing pressure and weakness in its mainstay market, North America, which declined 1.5% year on year.The slowdown was particularly sharp in high-tech and retail, which declined 17.3% and 7.7% year on year, respectively, in constant currency terms.Infosys CEO Salil Parekh said the weakness was driven by specific client situations rather than a broad-based slowdown across industries. “We have seen different client-specific situations in both retail and high-tech. This is not happening across all industries. We continue to see strong growth and discretionary spending in financial services, energy and utilities, and manufacturing,” he said.CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka said volumes remained subdued, while competitive intensity and clients’ higher productivity expectations had put pressure on pricing.Discretionary spending in retail and high-tech was also lower than anticipated, he said, adding that these factors had led to the guidance cut.Retail was additionally affected by a larger thirdparty component in the previous quarters, creating an unfavourable sequential comparison. While weakness in high-tech and retail was broadly similar across geographies, the impact was more pronounced in the US, Sanghrajka said.The company retained its operating margin guidance at 20%-22% for FY27.In dollar terms, Infosys’ revenue rose 1.2% sequentially and 1.3% year on year to $5.1 billion in the September quarter. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 1.2% sequentially and 1.5% year on year. AI was a bright spot, accounting for 10.5% of revenue and growing 29% sequentially, compared with 8.2% in the previous quarter, Parekh said.
Article Summary: The slowdown was particularly sharp in high-tech and retail, which declined 17.3% and 7.7% year on year. CEO Salil Parekh said the weakness was driven by specific client situations rather than a broad-based slowdown across industries.

Article Title: Driven by travel, outward transfers jump 6% to $2.7 billion
Article Text:
Travel accounted for 59.5% of total remittances, rising 11.4% from July to $1.6 billion.

MUMBAI: Outward remittances under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) rose 6% month-on-month to $2.7 billion in Aug 2026, driven by overseas student travel, business travel and payments for remote education, while investments in foreign equity and debt more than doubled from a year earlier.Travel accounted for 59.5% of total remittances, rising 11.4% from July to $1.6 billion. Within this, remittances for overseas education travel, including fees and hostel expenses, rose 28.5% to $855.5 million from $665.8 million.Business travel surged 365.4% to $51 million from $11 million, while other travel, including leisure trips and international credit card settlements, fell 7.4% to $713.8 million. Spending on pilgrimage travel declined 46% to $5.5 million and remittances for travel-related medical treatment fell 17.7% to $4.5 million.Investments in foreign equity and debt instruments fell 6.7% from July to $321.5 million but were 111.3% higher than in Aug 2025.Remittances for maintenance of close relatives declined 2.8% month-on-month to $275.4 million, while gifts fell 6.8% to $215.7 million. Both categories recorded annual increases of 1.2% and 13.3%, respectively.Remittances for remote and distance education rose 29.2% to $191.8 million from July but were 39.9% lower than a year earlier. This category covers educational services consumed remotely, including correspondence courses and online degree programmes, rather than expenses involving physical travel abroad.Deposits abroad rose 8.8% monthon-month to $50.8 million and were 18.8% higher year-on-year. Remittances for overseas property purchases fell 22.2% to $39.6 million from July but were 9.9% higher than a year earlier. Other remittances declined 13.3% to $8.1 million, while payments for remote medical treatment rose 23.2% to $4.8 million. Donations fell 34.2% to $0.5 million.
Article Summary: Travel accounted for 59.5% of total remittances, rising 11.4% from July to $1.6 billion. Investments in foreign equity and debt more than doubled from a year earlier. Remittances for maintenance of close relatives declined 2.8% month-on- month.

Article Title: Demand at home supporting growth momentum: RBI
Article Text:
The report said deficient rainfall in some regions could adversely affect kharif crop yields.

MUMBAI: RBI’s Oct 2026 State of the Economy report flagged rising inflation, geopolitical tensions and global financial volatility as key risks to India’s growth outlook, even as strong domestic demand, services activity and exports supported economic momentum.The report said headline CPI inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.5% in Sept from 4.8% in Aug, with price increases spreading across food, fuel and core items. Core inflation rose to 4.3%, while core inflation excluding precious metals reached 3.2%. WPI inflation climbed to 11.4% under the 2022-23 base series. The report highlighted early signs of inflation generalisation, with a rising share of CPI items recording inflation above 6%.The report said deficient rainfall in some regions could adversely affect kharif crop yields. However, rice and wheat stocks stood at 3.3 times the quarterly buffer norm as of Oct 1, providing a cushion against supply disruptions. Higher minimum support prices announced on Sept 30 for the 2027-28 rabi marketing season were intended to ensure remunerative prices and incentivise crop diversification.Globally, the IMF outlook remained subject to downside risks, including the West Asia conflict, trade tensions, high sovereign bond yields, elevated public debt and concerns over fiscal sustainability.The global growth projection for 2027 assumed the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz in March and a broad return to pre-war conditions by Oct 2027. The report identified positive technology shocks and gains from artificial intelligence as potential offsets to the global slowdown.The report highlighted mounting global financial risks as geopolitical frictions in West Asia intensified inflationary pressures and disrupted supply chains. Elevated sovereign bond yields in advanced economies raised concerns about fiscal sustainability and financial stability, particularly amid debt and fiscal pressures in France and the US.
Article Summary: RBI’s Oct 2026 State of the Economy report flagged rising inflation, geopolitical tensions and global financial volatility as key risks. The report said headline CPI inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.5% in Sept from 4.8% in Aug.

Article Title: Coforge revenue grew 40% in Q2; margin guidance raised to 16%
Article Text:
Sudhir Singh, CEO, Sudhir Singh

Bengaluru: Coforge’s revenue rose 40.1% year on year and 10.1% sequentially in dollar terms to $652.2 million in the September quarter. Organic revenue growth in constant currency (CC) terms was 3.8% sequentially.Operating margin expanded 134 basis points year on year to 16%, while remaining flat sequentially.The company raised its FY27 operating margin guidance to 16% from 15.5% and expects to expand it further to 17% next year.“The 10.1% sequential growth and 40.1% YoY growth in US dollar terms, a 3.8% sequential organic CC growth, a next twelve month signed order book of $2.38 billion, an order intake of over $1 billion and eight large deals, the most the firm has ever signed in a single quarter, have put us firmly on course to be the industry growth leader for the third year running,” said Coforge CEO Sudhir Singh.Order intake stood at $1 billion, while the executable order book for the next 12 months rose 45.4% year on year to $2.38 billion. The company signed eight large deals during the quarter.“We are raising our FY27 EBIT margin guidance from 15.5% to 16%. We expect to further improve our EBIT margin to 17% next year; and will be targeting to be among top three scaled IT services firms on margins while maintaining our growth momentum,” Singh said.The Americas accounted for 63.1% of revenue, followed by Europe, the Middle East and Africa at 24.6% and the rest of the world at 12.3%. Banking, financial services and insurance contributed 25.3% of revenue, while healthcare and high-tech accounted for 17.6%.Coforge’s headcount rose to 47,365 from 46,228 in the previous quarter. Attrition stood at 10.4% on a last-twelve-month basis, excluding its business process services workforce.
Article Summary: Coforge’s revenue rose 40.1% year on year to $652.2 million in the September quarter. Organic revenue growth in constant currency (CC) terms was 3.8% sequentially. The company raised its FY27 operating margin guidance to 16% from 15.5% and expects to expand it further to 17%.

Article Title: Business sentiment rebounds in Q2, but remains below year-ago levels: NCAER survey
Article Text:
The Business Confidence Index (BCI) rose to 107.8 in the second quarter from 99.8 in the preceding quarter

New Delhi: Business confidence in India improved in the July-September quarter of FY2026-27 after declining for four consecutive quarters amid prolonged geopolitical tensions, with expectations of higher production, domestic sales and exports lifting sentiment ahead of the festive season, according to a survey by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER).The Business Confidence Index (BCI) rose to 107.8 in the second quarter from 99.8 in the preceding quarter, the latest NCAER Business Expectations Survey showed. However, the index remained significantly below the 142.6 recorded in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.Conducted in September, the survey covered 502 firms of varying sizes across six cities — Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Mumbai and Pune.The improvement was broad-based, with the share of firms expecting economic conditions to improve over the next six months rising to 50% from 43% in Q1. Similarly, the proportion expecting their financial position to improve increased to 41% from 37%, while firms viewing the investment climate positively rose to 30% from 26%.Capacity utilisation sentiments also strengthened, with 94% of firms expecting utilisation to remain close to or above optimal levels, compared with 91% in the previous quarter.Confidence improved among both micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and large firms. The BCI for MSMEs increased to 100 from 93, while that for large firms rose to 120.3 from 111.6.“The data indicate a broad-based recovery in sentiments across both MSMEs and large firms,” said NCAER professor Bornali Bhandari, who led the survey.Growth expectations strengthened across key business indicators. The share of firms expecting production to increase over the next six months rose to 68% from 66%, while expectations of higher domestic sales climbed to 71% from 67%.Among exporting firms, the proportion anticipating an increase in finished-product exports rose to 62% from 55%. Expectations of higher raw material imports also jumped to 55% from 35%, signalling a possible pickup in business activity.Cost pressures showed signs of easing, with the share of firms expecting raw material costs to rise declining to 60% from 67%. However, hiring intentions remained subdued, with most firms expecting no change in employment over the next six months.
Article Summary: Business confidence in India improved in the July-September quarter of FY2026-27. Expectations of higher production, domestic sales and exports lifted sentiment. Confidence improved among both micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and large firms.

Article Title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global cybersecurity alert
Article Text:
Bengaluru:

Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert, potentially exposing millions of internet-facing services. In a separate advisory, PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk, adding to concerns around the widely used programming language.PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bug-fix release. The warning follows an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Aamir Lakhani, global director of threat intelligence and adversarial artificial intelligence research at Fortinet, said the flaws posed an urgent risk to organisations relying on websites, customer portals and other web applications.“Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed this week pose an urgent security and business continuity risk for organizations that depend on websites, customer portals, and other web applications,” Lakhani said.PHP is a server-side programming language used by widely deployed platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Companies can be exposed through commercial applications, hosting providers and embedded software components even if they do not develop PHP applications themselves.The potential scale of exposure is significant. Censys identified approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services reporting potentially affected PHP versions in its Oct 22 snapshot. These are service counts, not unique servers or organisations, and may include installations already patched through vendor updates.Saeed Abbasi, head of the Threat Research Unit and director of product at Qualys, said the company found 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organisations, with 73% deployed on internet-facing assets, putting them within reach of remote attackers.“Applying a patch alone will not be sufficient for systems running unsupported versions, where upgrading is the only viable long-term solution. The key takeaway is that nearly all PHP installations are either vulnerable or running unsupported versions,” he said.CloudSEK said Shodan identified 2.2 million internet-facing services displaying PHP information worldwide, with India ranking ninth at 53,400 services. Of 36,700 Indian services revealing their PHP versions, about 36,100 were unpatched, including 19,500 running versions that have reached end of life, said Akash Karthi, security researcher at CloudSEK.Upgrading to a patched PHP version and restarting all PHP processes is the only complete fix for the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. Systems running unsupported versions may require vendor-provided updates or migration to supported versions. Interim security measures can reduce exposure but cannot eliminate the risk.
Article Summary: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert. PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk. The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell.

Article Title: Oil on fire, Goa, Tamil Nadu cut VAT on jet fuel
Article Text:
Two key states on Friday finally relented by cutting VAT on aviation turbine fuel

NEW DELHI: Amid surging crude prices, two key states on Friday finally relented by cutting VAT on aviation turbine fuel (ATF). Tamil Nadu reduced the rate from 29% TO 16% at Chennai; and to 1% at all other airports in the state. Similarly, Goa has reduced VAT from 15% to 7%. Most other states had much earlier cut taxes on jet fuel as the same has been rising relentlessly since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb.Tamil Nadu industries minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana said on X Friday: “We are reducing VAT on aviation fuel for domestic airlines from 29% to 16% at Chennai Airport, and to just 1% at other airports across Tamil Nadu. By slashing this, we are taking a decisive step towards making air travel more accessible and our regional airports more competitive. Lower operating costs can encourage airlines to introduce new routes, increase flight frequencies and expand operations beyond Chennai… we are building an aviation ecosystem that connects more regions, unlocks economic potential and powers Tamil Nadu’s next phase of growth. ”Thanking Goa on X Friday, IndiGo said on X: “We sincerely thank Goa CM Pramod P Sawant for the progressive decision to rationalise VAT on ATF in the state.This is a welcome move towards strengthening the aviation ecosystem, enhancing air connectivity and supporting Goa’s vibrant tourism sector. We hope this progressive approach inspires others to consider similar measures, particularly at a time when ATF costs remain high, to help make air travel more accessible for customers. Thank you for your continued commitment to fostering growth and progress in aviation.”Airlines globally are finding it tough to remain airborne due to twin pressures of ATF price hikes and airspace closures. For Indian carriers, two other factors further aggravate the situation — rupee weakening with most costs like lease rentals and maintenance being dollar-denominated and closure of Pakistan airspace which has made the flights to and from west longer for them.The Federation of Indian Airlines (FIA), that has Air India, IndiGo and SpiceJet as members, had earlier this month warned govt they will be forced to cut flights on “unviable routes” as aviation turbine fuel prices are now at the highest level in a decade.“Fuel component historically constituted about 30% to 40% of airline operating costs. (It) has increased to about 55% to 60% under the prevailing circumstances. In addition, airspace restrictions have resulted in longer flight routes, leading to higher fuel consumption, increased crew costs, and lower aircraft utilisation. Airlines are also facing additional pressure from depreciation of the Indian rupee, as key expenses such as fuel, aircraft leases, maintenance, and insurance are US dollar denominated,” says a recent FIA SOS sent to the Union aviation ministry.FIA has urged an “urgent support to continue uninterrupted operations and provide air connectivity during these challenging periods.” It had sought ATF pricing on cost plus model; ATF excise duty relief; Key states to reduce VAT on ATF and extend concession on landing and parking charges. “Such measures would provide much-needed support to the aviation sector, help preserve affordable air travel for passengers, and enable airlines to continue contributing to India's economic growth and connectivity objectives despite the challenging operating environment. If timely relief is not available, the airlines may be compelled to withdraw from several unsustainable routes,” FIA letter says.The industry says the “unprecedented financial and operational challenges” “have severely strained airline liquidity and working capital, necessitating immediate got support.”
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu reduced the rate from 29% TO 16% at Chennai; and to 1% at all other airports in the state. Goa has reduced VAT from 15% to 7%. Most other states had much earlier cut taxes on jet fuel as the same has been rising relentlessly since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb.

Article Title: CJP’s Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde to face SEM court hearing today after skipping Delhi Police questioning
Article Text:
CJP activists Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, and Ajinkya Shinde are set to return to court this Friday

CJP activists miss Crime Branch questioning

SEM court orders release of CJP leaders from judicial custody

Why were CJP activists detained?





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) activists Saurav Das , Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde are expected to appear before a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court on Friday, even as the Delhi Police Crime Branch continues its investigation into the October 13 Jantar Mantar protest case.The three activists, who were summoned for questioning on Thursday but did not appear, have been asked to join the probe between 10 am and 4 pm, ahead of the court hearing scheduled for 3 pm.The Crime Branch had called the three activists to its Rajouri Garden office at noon on Thursday. However, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde did not appear before the investigating agency and sought additional time to join the probe.Police are expected to issue fresh notices to the activists. No fresh notice had been issued for Friday, but they have been asked to appear for questioning anytime between 10 am and 4 pm.If the activists decide to join the investigation on Friday, they are expected to appear before the Crime Branch before the SEM court hearing at 3 pm. Their appearance before the investigating agency, however, will depend on their decision.The latest developments follow an order by the SEM court directing the release of Das and Ranka from judicial custody after accepting their personal and surety bonds and recording written undertakings from them to maintain peace and abide by the law.SEM Ritu Raj directed both leaders to furnish personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each, which will remain in force until the conclusion of the enquiry.The court also instructed them to attend every hearing and comply with the conditions laid down in their bonds and undertakings.In their written undertakings, Das and Ranka pledged not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also agreed not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law.Any future demonstrations, they stated, would be conducted within the constitutional framework."Further judicial custody does not appear to be necessary at this stage, particularly after written undertakings before this Court," the SEM court observed while ordering their release.Das and Ranka were detained in connection with a protest held at Jantar Mantar on October 13. The site had been denotified as a designated protest venue.According to the police, the activists entered the area through private premises and allegedly violated conditions relating to the maintenance of peace.The case concerns the circumstances surrounding the protest and the alleged breach of the applicable restrictions.The SEM court has clarified that the enquiry into the matter will continue in accordance with the law, despite the release of the two activists from judicial custody.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: CJP activists Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, and Ajinkya Shinde are set to return to court this Friday. Delhi Police Crime Branch continues its investigation into the October 13 Jantar Mantar protest case. The three activists were summoned for questioning on Thursday but did not appear.

Article Title: Heavy rain lashes Chennai, schools shut in 4 districts
Article Text:
Heavy rain affected Chennai and nearby areas, prompting school closures as a precautionary measure.

The Regional Meteorological Centre reported significant rainfall across the city and adjoining districts.





CHENNAI: Heavy rain lashed Chennai and neighbouring districts overnight, prompting authorities to declare a holiday for schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu on Wednesday.Chennai collector S Malathi Helen and the collectors of the three neighbouring districts ordered the closures as a precautionary measure amid forecasts of further heavy showers.According to the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), weather stations at Meenambakkam and Nungambakkam recorded more than 10cm of rainfall as of 6am on Wednesday. Several parts of the city, including Taramani, Villivakkam and Nandanam, also received moderate to heavy showers.A low-pressure area is likely to develop over the southwest Bay of Bengal and the adjoining Tamil Nadu coast, bringing heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places across Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. The wet spell is expected to continue until Oct 26, while another low-pressure area may form over the Bay of Bengal around Oct 23.Meanwhile, the early-morning holiday announcement caught some government school kitchens off guard.Staff had begun preparing breakfast for students in Classes 1 to 8 under the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme before the closure order was issued.“The holiday was declared only around 6am. We started preparing breakfast around 5.30am. We are looking to distribute it to conservancy workers,” a headmaster said.District authorities said any decision on Thursday's closure would depend on the intensity of rainfall and a review of weather conditions on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu closed as a precautionary measure. Weather stations recorded more than 10cm of rainfall as of 6am on Wednesday. A low-pressure area is likely to develop over the southwest Bay of Bengal and the adjoining Tamil Nadu coast.

Article Title: Trump eases tariffs on Canadian imports weeks before US midterms, offering relief to Maine
Article Text:
The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Collins seeks relief for Maine businesses

Trade tensions strain US-Canada ties

US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports, with the move coming just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine, a state whose economy has been affected by the trade dispute with Canada.The White House said the changes would remove tariffs on certain products, including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment". However, the administration will also introduce tariffs on other goods, including carpets, certain valves and waste products. The new measures will take effect on October 30.Collins said she had "secured" the exemptions for products important to Maine's agricultural sector, including blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed producers.Collins, who faces a strong challenge from a Democratic candidate, said farmers in her state depend on supplies from Canada that are difficult or expensive to source elsewhere.She said many farmers "rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."The senator's intervention comes as Democrats target her seat in their bid to take control of Congress from Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections.Maine shares a border with Canada, and businesses in the state have felt the effects of Trump's trade policies.The partial tariff relief could ease costs for some businesses, although the introduction of duties on other Canadian products means the changes will not benefit every sector.Also Read: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean The United States and Canada have closely connected economies, with roughly 70 per cent of Canadian exports going to the US. Trade relations have deteriorated since negotiations between the two countries broke down in August, prompting Trump to impose a fresh round of tariffs.Earlier US duties on Canadian cars, steel, aluminium and lumber have hurt businesses, contributed to job losses and weighed on economic growth. Canada entered a technical recession this year after its economy contracted for two consecutive quarters.The tariffs imposed after the collapse of trade talks affected goods worth around $20 billion, equivalent to 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the US. The targeted products ranged from hockey sticks to cement.Since returning to office for his second term, Trump has imposed extensive tariffs on imports from both allies and rivals, arguing that other countries have taken advantage of the United States.His administration has also linked some threatened tariffs to broader political and foreign policy goals.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports. The move comes just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine. The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Article Title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
Article Text:
Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert.

India ranked ninth globally among services displaying PHP information.

BENGALURU: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert, potentially exposing millions of internet-facing services. In a separate advisory, PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk, adding to concerns over the widely used programming language.PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Aamir Lakhani, global director of threat intelligence and adversarial artificial intelligence research at Fortinet, said: “Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed this week pose an urgent security and business continuity risk for organizations that depend on websites, customer portals, and other web applications.PHP is a server-side programming language used by widely deployed platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Companies can be exposed through commercial applications, hosting providers and embedded software components even if they do not develop PHP applications themselves.The potential scale of exposure is significant. Censys identified approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services reporting potentially affected PHP versions in its Oct 22 snapshot. These are service counts, not unique servers or organisations, and may include installations already patched through vendor updates.Saeed Abbasi, head of the Threat Research Unit and director of product at Qualys, said the company found 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organisations, with 73% deployed on internet-facing assets, putting them within reach of remote attackers. “Applying a patch alone will not be sufficient for systems running unsupported versions, where upgrading is the only viable long-term solution. The key takeaway is that nearly all PHP installations are either vulnerable or running unsupported versions,” he said.CloudSEK said Shodan identified 2.2 million internet-facing services displaying PHP information worldwide, with India ranking ninth at 53,400 services. Of 36,700 Indian services revealing their PHP versions, about 36,100 were unpatched, including 19,500 running versions that have reached end of life, said Akash Karthi, a security researcher at CloudSEK.
Article Summary: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert. In a separate advisory, PHP urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk. The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell.

Article Title: Amex to cut 3,500 jobs globally despite raising 2026 profit forecast
Article Text:
American Express announced it will be laying off around 3,500 employees worldwide

American Express is cutting about 5 percent of its global workforce, affecting around 3,500 employees, as chief executive officer Steve Squeri seeks to control rising expenses and streamline operations, even as the company raises its full-year earnings forecast after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter results.According to Bloomberg, Squeri told Bloomberg TV that the company has around 78,000 employees globally. Speaking during a call with analysts on Friday, he said the job cuts were aimed at making the company more agile and efficient by reducing management layers and speeding up decision-making.The move comes amid a broader wave of workforce reductions across the financial services sector, with companies seeking to improve efficiency and, in some cases, citing the growing use of artificial intelligence.Barclays said this week it would eliminate 5,000 jobs, while HSBC is planning reductions across its UK wealth-management business. Citigroup has also been reducing its workforce.Amex announced the cuts after reporting adjusted earnings of $4.68 per share for the third quarter, beating the average analyst estimate of $4.49 in a Bloomberg survey. The company also raised its full-year 2026 earnings forecast to between $18.30 and $18.60 per share, from its earlier projection of $17.30 to $17.90.However, the company's billed business, which measures transactions on its credit cards and other products, came in at $454 billion during the quarter, below the average analyst estimate of $456.9 billion. Amex said it had exited certain small-business co-brand deals, affecting the results.Analysts at Truist Securities, including Brian Foran, described the results as mixed, noting that the earnings beat and improved guidance were positive but that slower growth in billed business was a disappointment.The company reported third-quarter expenses of $14.5 billion, an increase of about 9 percent, although the figure was below analysts' estimate of $14.8 billion. Rising costs have added to the pressure on management to improve operational efficiency while sustaining business growth.Amex's results were also affected by the sale of its equity interest in Global Business Travel Group Inc, which generated an after-tax gain of $751 million. The company used part of the proceeds to fund a $253 million after-tax restructuring charge linked to efficiency initiatives. The gain, net of the restructuring charge, was excluded from adjusted results.“Our business momentum continues, with strength in billings, new acquisitions and card member retention, and excellent credit quality,” Squeri said in a statement.The company has also been investing in its premium-card offerings. Last year, it introduced several new benefits for its Platinum card, and earlier this month announced a partnership with Airbnb that will allow certain luxury rentals booked through its travel site to qualify for cardholders' annual lodging credit.Chief financial officer Christophe Le Caillec had previously said marketing expenses were expected to rise by around 10 percent in the second half of 2026 compared with the same period last year.Separately, Amex faces a $350 million fine following enforcement actions by the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Reserve over alleged deficiencies in its anti-money-laundering systems. The company said the penalty would not affect its previously issued full-year 2026 earnings guidance or its 2027 outlook. The regulatory orders also do not impose an asset cap on the company.
Article Summary: Amex announced the cuts after reporting adjusted earnings of $4.68 per share for the third quarter. Chief executive officer Steve Squeri said the job cuts were aimed at making the company more agile and efficient by reducing management layers. The move comes amid a broader wave of workforce reductions across the financial services sector.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.

Article Title: Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs by 2026-end as AI takes on bigger role in bank's operations
Article Text:
Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs

Barclays plans to eliminate around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of this year as the British lender streamlines its operations and increases its investment in technology, including artificial intelligence (AI).The bank has already closed 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000. Around 60% of the reductions are expected to affect support functions, including developers, while operational and functional roles will account for most of the job losses.The move comes as Barclays approaches the end of a three-year cost-cutting programme focused primarily on its UK retail banking business. Its investment banking division is also affected.In its third-quarter earnings presentation on Thursday, the bank said it was “structurally reducing the cost base to generate capacity for investment.” It described the expected outcome as “organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI.”Barclays said AI was the "icing on the cake" of its wider modernisation strategy. Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts reflected significant investment in technology to simplify and improve the business.Barclays reported pre-tax profit of £2.3 billion ($3.1 billion) for the three months to September, up 12% from the same period a year earlier. The figure matched forecasts compiled by LSEG, although the results were also described as slightly below forecast.Group income stood at £7.4 billion, below analysts' estimate of £7.61 billion, while net interest income was broadly unchanged at £3.91 billion.The bank's CET1 capital ratio, a measure of financial solvency, edged down to 14.2% from 14.3% at the end of the second quarter. Return on tangible equity fell to 11.7% from 16.1%.Barclays shares were almost 1% lower less than an hour into the trading session. Economists are examining company results for evidence that spending on new technology, particularly AI, is improving day-to-day operations, boosting efficiency and reducing staffing requirements.Barclays' latest workforce reduction comes amid this wider scrutiny of how companies are using AI and whether the technology is delivering operational gains.
Article Summary: Barclays plans to eliminate around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of this year. The bank has already closed 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000. Around 60% of the reductions are expected to affect support functions.

Article Title: Meta Q3 results: Net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion, but legal charge hits operating income
Article Text:
Meta's Q3 net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion

Higher spending planned for AI infrastructure

Meta Platforms' net income more than tripled in the third quarter of 2026, rising 264 per cent year-on-year to $9.86 billion, as higher advertising revenue boosted its financial performance. However, a $9.89 billion legal charge pushed operating income down 37 per cent despite a 26 per cent increase in overall revenue.The company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in the same period last year. Net income stood at $2.71 billion a year earlier, while diluted earnings per share rose to $3.83 from $1.05.Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26 per cent from a year ago. The number of ad impressions across its family of applications increased 10 per cent, while the average price per advertisement rose 14 per cent year-on-year.Despite the increase in revenue and net income, operating income dropped to $12.99 billion from $20.54 billion in the year-ago quarter. Total costs and expenses climbed 68 per cent to $51.61 billion, reflecting, among other expenses, a $9.89 billion charge tied to an agreement with 52 US state attorneys general to resolve litigation concerning teen mental health and social media.Meta said that excluding this charge, operating income would have been $22.88 billion. Diluted earnings per share would have reached $7.40, rather than the reported $3.83.Meta expects revenue in the fourth quarter to be between $73 billion and $76 billion. It has also revised its full-year 2026 expense outlook upwards to $175-179 billion, taking the legal charge into account.The company has increased its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 to $135-145 billion, from the previous range of $130-145 billion. The spending is part of its continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and other business priorities.In the chief financial officer's outlook commentary, Meta said, “Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization.”The company said its spending on AI models and infrastructure was opening up additional revenue opportunities. However, it expects these investments to take longer to generate returns than its core business.“While these investments will take longer to generate returns than those in our core business, the breadth of monetization opportunities and internal efficiencies gives us confidence in their long-term potential,” the commentary said.Meta expects its AI investments, improvements in its models and new product launches to support strong overall revenue growth through 2027.The company is still working on its budget and capacity plans for next year as it continues to invest in AI infrastructure and pursue the revenue opportunities it expects these investments to create.
Article Summary: Meta Platforms' Q3 net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion. Company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in same period last year. Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26% from a year ago.
